page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 3,800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by 100 Gbps baseline network throughput. No hardware GPUs are included on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational efficiency in specialized and data-intensive tasks. The server scores in the top tier for PassMark CPU performance, PassMark database operations, and multi-core compilation workloads using Clang. Memory bandwidth reaches 167.06 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 67.91 GB/sec for large uncached writes, while Redis achieves 55.14 million SET operations per second. General synthetic single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, sit in the middle performance tier.

From an infrastructure perspective, bundling 3.8 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage and 100 Gbps networking provides significant data throughput without requiring external attachment overhead. However, achieving cost efficiency requires dense resource utilization across memory and I/O channels, as the high core and memory count incurs baseline commitments that may be uneconomical for bursty or lightly loaded systems.

The r6idn.16xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, real-time analytics platforms, distributed cache clusters, big data processing pipelines, and data-intensive transaction systems requiring large memory capacity and fast scratch disk I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services r6idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz. It includes 512 GB of DDR4 system memory, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and integrates 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with 100 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark testing exhibits strong throughput in database transactions, large-scale software compilation, and PassMark computational tests, alongside steady mid-tier general single-core performance. The bundled high-speed local storage and broad network pipe reduce the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads. This instance profile is engineered for memory-heavy transactional databases, in-memory distributed caches, and large data-processing applications.
